text:
Maya K.: heads-up — ran into recurring issue where ephemeral KMS tokens used by CI to decrypt test fixtures are showing up as SAST/secret-scan hits in premerge scans. thinking out loud on a small playbook to: 1) ensure reviewers can validate ephemeral creds are scoped and time-limited; 2) confirm audit logs show decrypt events; 3) automatic suppression for known test fixtures. any concerns?

Jordan L.: can you paste an example of the finding? is it the secret scanner or the SAST rule?

Maya K.: this one is secret-scan (gitleaks) flagged a base64 blob in tests/helpers/fixtures that contains an encrypted payload. not a plaintext key, but the CI helper uses `gcloud kms decrypt --plaintext-file` during tests. snippet:
```bash
# in CI step
gcloud kms decrypt --ciphertext-file=fixtures/sample.enc --plaintext-file=fixtures/sample.json --location=global --keyring=ci-keys --key=ephemeral-test-key
```
Scanner just flags the ciphertext blob as potential secret since it's long base64.

Samir P.: if the ciphertext blob is static in the repo that's an issue. but if it's regenerated at build and rotated frequently maybe we can suppress. Do we have an owners file for fixtures? Who approves suppressions?

Maya K.: currently no owners. Proposal: add an OWNERS entry under tests/fixtures and require a security sign-off label `sec:fixtures-ok` before suppression is allowed. Also record in audit log: decrypt event + CI job id. That way reviewers can quickly check.

Lexi (sec-eng): sounds reasonable. For audit logging we should require KMS audit entries include principal and job id. On GCP, we can match `protoPayload.methodName":"google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt"` plus `requestMetadata.requestAttributes.callerIp`. We can add a quick grep snippet for reviewers:
```bash
gcloud logging read \"protoPayload.methodName=\\\"google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt\\\" AND resource.labels.job_id=\\\"${CI_JOB_ID}\\\"\" --limit=50
```

Jordan L.: for the premerge scanner rule, can we add a rule whitelist that matches `fixtures/*.enc` and only allows it if PR has `sec:fixtures-ok` label? CI can gate that label via a bot check.

Maya K.: exactly. CI flow suggestion:
1) premerge scan marks hit but not block if path matches `tests/fixtures/**` and PR has no `sec:fixtures-ok` label -> comment to ask for owner review.
2) owner inspects audit log and PR, if ok adds `sec:fixtures-ok` and `ci-bot` will add a `suppress:fixtures` metadata to the scanner database.
3) second run of scanner respects suppress metadata and won't fail PR.

Samir P.: need to be careful with race conditions and misuse. Add an expiration to suppressions (e.g., 30d) and require re-review. Also record suppressions in a central Audit spreadsheet + the ticket.

Lexi (sec-eng): we should formalize as a mini playbook in docs: short checklist for reviewers (validate principal, check KMS decrypt log, confirm fixture owner, add label, check expiration). I can draft a PR to docs. Also add a separate path for DAST fuzzing artifacts which may differ.

Maya K.: thanks. I'll open two PRs: OWNERS file under tests/fixtures and a CI change to implement label gating + scanner suppression writeback. tagging @Jordan L. and @Samir P. for review. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: Started CI run 37892 for branch maya/fixture-playbook

oncall-bot: Deployment window reminder — if the fix touches infra configs, schedule during maintenance window.

Jordan L.: ack, will review by EOD. One more ask: can we add a quick `sast` note in PR template to remind authors to mark fixture PRs with `sec:fixtures-rationale` describing why the encrypted artifact must be checked in.

Maya K.: will add that to the PR template. Thanks everyone — I'll post the draft playbook link once PRs exist.
